entities.name: Battle of Tabouk
entities.label: EventWindow
entities.summary:
The Battle of Tabouk was a pivotal military expedition led by the Prophet Muhammad in 630 CE, marking a significant turning point in the Muslim conquests of Arabia. This event occurred in the context of the early Islamic expansion and the Prophet's campaigns to unify the Arabian Peninsula under a single, monotheistic faith. The expedition's outcome solidified Muhammad's authority and paved the way for the eventual unification of the Arabian tribes under Islam.

The Battle of Tabouk was a well-planned military campaign, carried out during the month of Shawwal in 630 CE. It involved a large force of approximately 3,000 soldiers, primarily drawn from the tribes of Quraysh and Hudhayl. The expedition's objective was to intercept and defeat the Christian tribes of the region, who had been raiding Muslim caravans and disrupting trade routes. The battle itself was relatively bloodless, with few casualties reported on either side. Despite some internal conflicts and logistical challenges, the expedition was ultimately successful in its objectives, leading to the strengthening of Muslim authority in the region.

The legacy of the Battle of Tabouk has been profound, with its impact felt far beyond the immediate region. The unification of the Arabian tribes under Islam had a lasting impact on the course of world history, shaping the development of Islamic civilization and its interactions with other cultures. The event also marked a significant milestone in the life of the Prophet Muhammad, cementing his reputation as a military leader and a unifying force for the Arabian people. The battle's outcome has been remembered for centuries as a testament to the power of faith and the importance of standing up for one's beliefs.
